text: The core of electrical engineering and its automation research lies in the entire life cycle of "electricity": from power generation (such as thermal, hydropower, wind power, and solar power generation), power transmission (high-voltage transmission networks), power distribution (urban power grids, industrial power distribution systems), to the control of power equipment at the power consumption end (such as motors, electrical appliances), power system automation (smart grids, dispatching systems), as well as fields related to electronic information processing and automation control involving electricity. With the development of technologies such as new energy, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things, this major has expanded from the traditional power system to emerging fields such as smart grids, new energy vehicles, power electronics, and robot control, featuring the cross-characteristics of strong and weak electricity, theory and practice, as well as traditional and cutting-edge.
